We need to understand why tests not found. The test class uses JUnit 5 annotations like @Test, @Before, etc., but they are commented out incorrectly? Actually they used @BeforeAll, @BeforeEach but commented out with //, and also @ExtendWith etc. The test class is package-private (no public) and class name ends with _Test. JUnit 5 discovers tests in any class annotated with @Test methods, but need to be public? In JUnit Jupiter, test classes and methods can be package-private. However the test runner didn't find any tests. Possibly because the test class is not annotated with @TestInstance? Not needed. The issue is that the test methods are not static? Not needed.

But the test class is missing import for JUnit 5's annotations? They used org.junit.Test which is JUnit 4. In JUnit 5, @Test is org.junit.jupiter.api.Test. The runner includes both JUnit Jupiter and Vintage. Since they imported JUnit 4 @Test, the test runner will treat them as JUnit 4 tests, but the class uses JUnit 4 @Before etc. However they commented out @BeforeAll and @BeforeEach, using JUnit 5 names but commented. They used @Before and @BeforeClass? Actually they imported org.junit.Before and org.junit.BeforeClass but those are JUnit 4. They used static void setupBeforeAll() annotated with // @BeforeAll (commented). So no @BeforeClass. So the test class has no @BeforeClass or @Before methods, but that's fine.

But the test runner didn't find any tests. Maybe because the class is not public and JUnit 4 requires public class? JUnit 4 requires public class and public methods. The class is package-private (default) and methods are package-private (no modifier). JUnit 4 requires public class and public methods annotated with @Test. So they are not discovered. JUnit Jupiter can handle non-public, but they used JUnit 4 @Test, so it's using Vintage engine. Vintage requires public class and methods. Therefore no tests found.

Solution: Change imports to JUnit Jupiter's @Test, @BeforeEach, @BeforeAll, and make class public (or keep default but JUnit Jupiter can handle). Also need to annotate methods with @BeforeAll static and @BeforeEach.

Also need to fix the test code to use proper imports and maybe remove commented annotations.

Thus corrected code: make class public, import org.junit.jupiter.api.*; remove JUnit 4 imports. Use @BeforeAll static void setupBeforeAll() and @BeforeEach void setupBeforeEach(). Also need to adjust any usage of @BeforeClass etc.

Also need to adjust numericIndicator.stddev( barCount ) returning NumericIndicator; need to ensure that getUnstableBars method exists.

But the code itself may compile fine.

Let's rewrite the test class accordingly.

Also need to import Duration, ZonedDateTime etc.

Make sure to use DecimalNum.ZERO constant; that's fine.

Add necessary imports.

Let's produce corrected code.
